title: One coordinate enlargement with countably generated projective quotient
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], $M$ an $A$-module, $I$ a set and $(Q_i)_{i\in I}$ countably generated projective $B$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Fix a $B$-linear isomorphism $\theta:B\otimes_A M\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{i\in I}Q_i$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. For $H\subseteq I$ let $D_H$ be the coordinate submodule of families vanishing outside $H$ [def-trf-coordinate-submodule]. For an $A$-submodule $W\subseteq M$, put $T(W)=\theta(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_A W\to B\otimes_A M))$, with the map induced by inclusion. Let $U\subseteq M$ and $H\subseteq I$ satisfy $T(U)=D_H$, and let $x\in M\setminus U$. There exist an $A$-submodule $V\subseteq M$ and $J\subseteq I\setminus H$ such that $U\subseteq V$, $x\in V$, $T(V)=D_{H\cup J}$ and $V/U$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] is countably generated and projective over $A$. Moreover the canonical map $B\otimes_A(V/U)\to B\otimes_A(M/U)$ is injective; under the isomorphism $B\otimes_A(M/U)\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I\setminus H}Q_i$ induced by $\theta$ and projection to the remaining coordinates, its image is the $J$-coordinate submodule. Countably generated means spanned by an at most countable subset using finite linear combinations. No finite-generation or finite-presentation hypothesis on $M$ or $U$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, successor paragraph: quotient tensor identification, adapted submodule, countable projectivity descent, and lifting the coordinate image to the inverse image in M (old proof steps 2, 5, 6 and the invariant in 7)

proof.text: Put $L=M/U$ and let $q:M\to L$ be the quotient map. Faithful flatness implies that $B$ is flat over $A$. Tensor right exactness applied to $U\to M\to L\to0$ gives a surjection $q_B:B\otimes_A M\to B\otimes_A L$ with kernel the tensor image of $U$. By the hypothesis $T(U)=D_H$, this kernel is $\theta^{-1}(D_H)$. Projection $\pi_H:\bigoplus_{i\in I}Q_i\to\bigoplus_{i\in I\setminus H}Q_i$ is surjective, with kernel $D_H$: extend a finite-support family by zero to obtain a lift, and check the kernel coordinatewise. Consequently $\rho(q_B(z))=\pi_H(\theta(z))$ defines a $B$-linear isomorphism $\rho:B\otimes_A L\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{i\in I\setminus H}Q_i$. It is well-defined because two lifts differ by $\theta^{-1}(D_H)$; it is injective by the same kernel calculation and surjective by the two surjections.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, successor paragraph (using Tags 05A8, lemma-adapted-submodule, and 05A6, lemma-ffdescent-countable-projectivity)

proof.text: The cyclic submodule $C=Aq(x)\subseteq L$ is countably generated. Apply the adapted-submodule lemma to $A\to B$, the module $L$, the decomposition $\rho$, and $C$. Every remaining $Q_i$ is countably generated by hypothesis; this lemma requires neither flatness nor projectivity. It gives a countably generated $P\subseteq L$ containing $q(x)$ and a subset $J\subseteq I\setminus H$ such that $\rho(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_A P\to B\otimes_A L))$ is exactly the $J$-coordinate submodule.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, successor paragraph (using Tags 05A8, lemma-adapted-submodule, and 05A6, lemma-ffdescent-countable-projectivity)

proof.text: Flat tensoring preserves the injection $P\hookrightarrow L$. Hence $B\otimes_A P$ is isomorphic, by restricting $\rho$, to the $J$-coordinate submodule. Restriction to $J$ and extension by zero identify that submodule with $\bigoplus_{j\in J}Q_j$. This direct sum is projective, since every $Q_j$ is projective; projectivity transfers along the displayed isomorphism. If $S\subseteq P$ is a countable spanning subset, then $\{1\otimes s:s\in S\}$ spans $B\otimes_A P$: expand each second tensor factor in $S$ and move its $A$-coefficients to the first factor. Thus the scalar extension is countably generated and projective. Countable projectivity descent for the faithfully flat map $A\to B$ now proves that $P$ is countably generated and projective over $A$.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, successor paragraph (using Tags 05A8, lemma-adapted-submodule, and 05A6, lemma-ffdescent-countable-projectivity)

proof.text: Define $V=q^{-1}(P)\subseteq M$. Then $U\subseteq V$ and $x\in V$. The map $q|_V:V\to P$ is surjective: lift any $p\in P$ along $q$, and its lift lies in $V$ by definition. Its kernel is $U$. The formula $v+U\mapsto q(v)$ gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $\alpha:V/U\xrightarrow{\sim}P$; the inverse sends $p$ to the class of any lift, independently of the choice since differences lie in $U$. Countable generators pull back along $\alpha$, and projectivity transfers along $\alpha$. Therefore $V/U$ is countably generated and projective.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, successor paragraph (using Tags 05A8, lemma-adapted-submodule, and 05A6, lemma-ffdescent-countable-projectivity)

proof.text: Let $E=\theta(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_A V\to B\otimes_A M))$. Since $U\subseteq V$, $D_H\subseteq E$. Tensor right exactness for the surjection $V\to P$ shows that $B\otimes_A V\to B\otimes_A P$ is surjective. On pure tensors the maps satisfy $\pi_H\theta(b\otimes v)=\rho(b\otimes q(v))$. Thus $\pi_H(E)$ is exactly the $J$-coordinate submodule in the remaining coordinates. For any submodule $E$ containing $\ker\pi_H=D_H$, one has $E=\pi_H^{-1}(\pi_H(E))$: if $\pi_H(z)=\pi_H(e)$ with $e\in E$, then $z-e\in D_H\subseteq E$. A family projects into the $J$-coordinate submodule precisely when it vanishes outside $H\cup J$. Therefore $E=D_{H\cup J}$, proving $T(V)=D_{H\cup J}$.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, successor paragraph (using Tags 05A8, lemma-adapted-submodule, and 05A6, lemma-ffdescent-countable-projectivity)

proof.text: The canonical map $V/U\to M/U=L$ is the composite of $\alpha$ with the inclusion $P\hookrightarrow L$. It is injective, as is its tensor with $B$ by flat tensoring. Tensoring $\alpha$ gives an isomorphism with inverse the tensor of $\alpha^{-1}$ (verify the composites on pure tensors). Under this isomorphism the image of $B\otimes_A(V/U)\to B\otimes_A L$ is the image of $B\otimes_A P\to B\otimes_A L$, which step 2 identified via $\rho$ with the $J$-coordinate submodule. The isomorphism $\rho$ is exactly the one induced by $\theta$ and projection to the remaining coordinates in the statement, by its defining formula in step 1.

lean.statement: theorem exists_coordinate_projective_successor {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B] {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] {I : Type t} {Q : I → Type s} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (Q i)] [∀ i, Module B (Q i)] (hQcount : ∀ i, ∃ c : Set (Q i), c.Countable ∧ Submodule.span B c = ⊤) (hQproj : ∀ i, Module.Projective B (Q i)) (θ : B ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[B] ⨁ i : I, Q i) (U : Submodule A M) (H : Set I) (hU : LinearMap.range (θ.toLinearMap.comp (U.subtype.baseChange B)) = DirectSum.coordinateSubmodule B I Q H) (x : M) (hx : x ∉ U) : ∃ (V : Submodule A M) (J : Set I), J ⊆ Hᶜ ∧ U ≤ V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ LinearMap.range (θ.toLinearMap.comp (V.subtype.baseChange B)) = DirectSum.coordinateSubmodule B I Q (H ∪ J) ∧ (∃ c : Set (V ⧸ U.comap V.subtype), c.Countable ∧ Submodule.span A c = ⊤) ∧ Module.Projective A (V ⧸ U.comap V.subtype) ∧ Function.Injective (((U.comap V.subtype).mapQ U V.subtype le_rfl).baseChange B) ∧ ∃ ρ : B ⊗[A] (M ⧸ U) ≃ₗ[B] ⨁ i : {i : I // i ∉ H}, Q i.val, (∀ (b : B) (m : M) (i : {i : I // i ∉ H}), ρ (b ⊗ₜ[A] U.mkQ m) i = θ (b ⊗ₜ[A] m) i.val) ∧ LinearMap.range (ρ.toLinearMap.comp (((U.comap V.subtype).mapQ U V.subtype le_rfl).baseChange B)) = DirectSum.coordinateSubmodule B {i : I // i ∉ H} (fun i : {i : I // i ∉ H} ↦ Q i.val) {i : {i : I // i ∉ H} | i.val ∈ J}
